newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilts down on higher call money rates.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilts down on higher call money rates.

text.p: * Indian government security prices down on higher call money rates but trade dull, dealers said.
* Call money traded in a 9.5-10.5 percent range on Monday against weekend close of 9.0-9.5. Call money was below 1.0 percent for most of April.
* Announcement of a new loan for five year bonds, and draining liquidity through last Wednesday's state government bond issue seen contributing to bearish sentiment, they said.
Bonds worth 25 billion rupees were offered for sale on April 30 - the Reserve Bank of India accepted bids for 53.81 billion with bids from some outlying centres bids still to arrive.
The federal government auctions 30 billion rupees of five-year bonds on Friday.
* Liquidity is still not tight but market sentiment is definitely down, said a dealer at a state-run bank.

* In latest deals, the 13.50 percent 1998 stock traded at 102.25 rupees against weekend 102.65, the 13.50 percent 1997 down to 101.40 from 101.51 and the 13.70 percent 1999 down to 103.65 from 104.10, dealers said.
